@startuml homelab-network-architecture
!theme plain
title Homelab Network & Service Architecture

' ============================================================================
' Style Configuration
' ============================================================================
skinparam {
    BackgroundColor white
    ComponentStyle rectangle
    PackageStyle frame
    DefaultFontName Monospace
    DefaultFontSize 11
    NoteFontSize 10
    ArrowColor #666666
    ComponentBorderColor #333333
    PackageBorderColor #555555
    DatabaseBorderColor #555555
    CloudBorderColor #555555
}

' Colors by category
!$CORE_COLOR = "#E8F5E9"
!$DASHBOARD_COLOR = "#E3F2FD"
!$PHOTOS_COLOR = "#FFF3E0"
!$MEDIA_COLOR = "#FCE4EC"
!$MONITORING_COLOR = "#F3E5F5"
!$INFRA_COLOR = "#ECEFF1"

' ============================================================================
' External Networks
' ============================================================================
cloud "Internet" as internet {
    [Cloudflare Tunnel] as cf_tunnel
    note right of cf_tunnel : Public domains\n*.rambtech.dev
}

' ============================================================================
' Home LAN (192.168.1.0/24 - vmbr0)
' ============================================================================
package "Home LAN\n192.168.1.0/24 (vmbr0)" as lan #FFFDE7 {
    node "FIOS Router\n192.168.1.1" as router

    rectangle "LAN Clients" as lan_clients {
        [Desktop/Laptop]
        [Mobile Devices]
        [Smart TVs]
    }
}

' ============================================================================
' Proxmox Host
' ============================================================================
node "Proxmox VE (homelab)\n192.168.1.215 (vmbr0)\n10.100.0.1 (vmbr1)" as proxmox #ECEFF1 {

    ' ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    ' Container Network (10.100.0.0/16 - vmbr1)
    ' ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    package "Container Network\n10.100.0.0/16 (vmbr1)" as container_net {

        ' ====================================================================
        ' Core Services (100-149) -> 10.100.1.x
        ' ====================================================================
        package "Core Services (10.100.1.x)" as core $CORE_COLOR {

            component "LXC 101: Network Services\n10.100.1.101\nLAN: 192.168.1.196" as network_svc {
                [AdGuard Home :80/:53]
                [Tailscale Exit Node]
            }

            component "LXC 102: PBS\n10.100.1.102" as pbs {
                [Proxmox Backup :8007]
            }
        }

        ' ====================================================================
        ' Dashboards & Auth (200-249) -> 10.100.2.x
        ' ====================================================================
        package "Dashboards & Auth (10.100.2.x)" as dashboards $DASHBOARD_COLOR {
            component "LXC 200: Traefik\n10.100.2.200\nLAN: 192.168.1.235" as traefik {
                [Traefik :443 (websecure)]
                [Traefik :80 (web/tunnel)]
                [Dashboard :8080]
            }

            component "LXC 201: Dashboards\n10.100.2.201" as dashboard_apps {
                [Homepage :3000]
                [Dashy :4001]
                [Glances :61208]
            }

            component "LXC 202: Authelia\n10.100.2.202" as authelia {
                [Authelia :9091]
                [Redis :6379]
            }
        }

        ' ====================================================================
        ' Photos (300-349) -> 10.100.3.x
        ' ====================================================================
        package "Photos (10.100.3.x)" as photos $PHOTOS_COLOR {
            component "LXC 303: Immich Importer\n10.100.3.103" as importer {
                [Photo Import Scripts]
            }

            component "LXC 304: Immich\n10.100.3.104\nLAN: 192.168.1.222" as immich {
                [Immich Server :2283]
                [Machine Learning :3003]
                [PostgreSQL :5432]
                [Redis :6379]
            }
        }

        ' ====================================================================
        ' Media - Streaming (400-449) -> 10.100.4.x
        ' ====================================================================
        package "Media Streaming (10.100.4.x)" as media $MEDIA_COLOR {
            component "LXC 401: Jellyfin\n10.100.4.101\nLAN: 192.168.1.226" as jellyfin {
                [Jellyfin :8096]
                [Jellystat :3000]
                [Jellyseerr :5055]
            }

            component "LXC 402: Media Management\n10.100.4.102" as arr_stack {
                [Sonarr :8989]
                [Radarr :7878]
                [Lidarr :8686]
                [Prowlarr :9696]
                [Bazarr :6767]
                [qBittorrent :8080]
                [SABnzbd :8085]
            }
        }

        ' ====================================================================
        ' Monitoring & AI (500-549) -> 10.100.5.x
        ' ====================================================================
        package "Monitoring & AI (10.100.5.x)" as monitoring $MONITORING_COLOR {
            component "LXC 500: Monitoring\n10.100.5.100" as mon_stack {
                [Prometheus :9090]
                [Grafana :3000]
                [Alertmanager :9093]
                [Uptime Kuma :3001]
                [ntfy :8080]
                [Loki :3100]
                [Alloy :4317/:4318/:12345]
            }

            component "LXC 501: OpenWebUI\n10.100.5.101" as openwebui {
                [OpenWebUI :3000]
                [Ollama :11434]
            }

            component "LXC 502: n8n\n10.100.5.102" as n8n {
                [n8n :5678]
            }
        }
    }

    ' ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    ' Storage
    ' ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    database "ZFS Storage" as storage {
        [tank/data/library]
        [tank/backups]
        [nvme-containers]
    }
}

' ============================================================================
' Traffic Flow Connections
' ============================================================================

' Internet -> Cloudflare -> Traefik
internet --> cf_tunnel
cf_tunnel --> traefik : "Public traffic\n(web entrypoint :80)"

' LAN -> Router -> Traefik (via LAN IP)
router --> traefik : "LAN traffic\n192.168.1.235:443"
lan_clients --> router

' DNS Resolution
lan_clients ..> network_svc : "DNS queries\n192.168.1.196:53"

' Traefik reverse proxy to services
traefik --> dashboard_apps : "homepage/dashy"
traefik --> authelia : "auth forwarding"
traefik --> jellyfin : "jellyfin/requests"
traefik --> immich : "photos"
traefik --> mon_stack : "grafana/prometheus"
traefik --> openwebui : "ai"
traefik --> n8n : "n8n"
traefik --> arr_stack : "sonarr/radarr/etc"
traefik --> pbs : "pbs"

' Authelia protects services
authelia ..> dashboard_apps : "ForwardAuth"
authelia ..> mon_stack : "ForwardAuth"

' Media flow
arr_stack --> jellyfin : "Media files"
jellyfin --> storage : "/data/library"
immich --> storage : "Photo storage"
pbs --> storage : "Backups"

' Monitoring
mon_stack ..> proxmox : "OTLP metrics"

' DLNA/Casting (via LAN IP)
lan_clients ..> jellyfin : "DLNA\n192.168.1.226"
lan_clients ..> immich : "Mobile sync\n192.168.1.222"

' ============================================================================
' Legend
' ============================================================================
legend bottom right
|= Network |= Range |= Purpose |
| vmbr0 | 192.168.1.0/24 | Home LAN |
| vmbr1 | 10.100.0.0/16 | Container network |
|= IP Scheme |= LXC Range |= Category |
| 10.100.1.x | 100-149 | Core services |
| 10.100.2.x | 200-249 | Dashboards & Auth |
| 10.100.3.x | 300-349 | Photos |
| 10.100.4.x | 400-449 | Media Streaming |
| 10.100.5.x | 500-549 | Monitoring & AI |
endlegend

@enduml

1→# Homelab IaC Architecture Design
     2→
     3→## Vision: Modular Service Deployment with Automatic Bindings
     4→
     5→### Problem Statement
     6→
     7→- Manual LXC creation via Proxmox UI or community scripts (xterm)
     8→- Manual Traefik route configuration
     9→- Manual Cloudflare tunnel/DNS setup
    10→- No standardized way to add new services
    11→- Hard to track what's running where
    12→
    13→### Solution: Two-Tier Service Model with OpenTofu
    14→
    15→```
    16→┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    17→│                           SERVICE TYPES                                     │
    18→├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    19→│                                                                             │
    20→│  CORE SERVICES (Long-lived, foundational)                                   │
    21→│  ├── traefik        → Ingress, TLS termination                              │
    22→│  ├── cloudflared    → Public tunnel                                         │
    23→│  ├── adguard        → DNS + ad blocking                                     │
    24→│  ├── tailscale      → Mesh VPN                                              │
    25→│  ├── pulse, arcane  → Container management                                  │
    26→│  └── postgres       → Shared database (optional)                            │
    27→│                                                                             │
    28→│  APP SERVICES (User-facing applications)                                    │
    29→│  ├── immich         → Photo management                                      │
    30→│  ├── openwebui      → AI chat interface                                     │
    31→│  ├── jellyfin       → Media streaming                                       │
    32→│  ├── homepage       → Dashboard                                             │
    33→│  └── ... any new service                                                    │
    34→│                                                                             │
    35→└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    36→```
    37→
    38→## Architecture: Module-Based IaC
    39→
    40→```
    41→tofu/
    42→├── main.tf                    # Root configuration
    43→├── providers.tf               # Proxmox, Cloudflare providers
    44→├── variables.tf               # Global variables
    45→│
    46→├── modules/
    47→│   ├── lxc-base/              # Base LXC container module
    48→│   │   ├── main.tf
    49→│   │   ├── variables.tf
    50→│   │   └── outputs.tf
    51→│   │
    52→│   ├── docker-host/           # LXC + Docker/Podman setup
    53→│   │   ├── main.tf            # Calls lxc-base + provisions Docker
    54→│   │   ├── variables.tf
    55→│   │   └── outputs.tf
    56→│   │
    57→│   ├── traefik-route/         # Traefik ingress binding
    58→│   │   ├── main.tf            # Creates route file, syncs to Traefik
    59→│   │   ├── variables.tf       # service_name, port, domain, middlewares
    60→│   │   └── outputs.tf         # route_url
    61→│   │
    62→│   ├── cloudflare-expose/     # Public exposure via tunnel or DNS
    63→│   │   ├── main.tf            # DNS record or tunnel ingress rule
    64→│   │   ├── variables.tf       # domain, expose_type (tunnel/ddns)
    65→│   │   └── outputs.tf         # public_url
    66→│   │
    67→│   └── proxmox-notes/         # Update LXC description/notes
    68→│       ├── main.tf            # pct set -description via SSH
    69→│       └── variables.tf
    70→│
    71→├── core/                      # Core service definitions
    72→│   ├── traefik.tf
    73→│   ├── cloudflared.tf
    74→│   ├── adguard.tf
    75→│   └── tailscale.tf
    76→│
    77→└── apps/                      # Application definitions
    78→    ├── immich.tf
    79→    ├── openwebui.tf
    80→    ├── jellyfin.tf
    81→    └── homepage.tf
    82→```
    83→
    84→## Key Concept: Composable Service Module
    85→
    86→When you want to add a new service, you just define it like this:
    87→
    88→```hcl
    89→# tofu/apps/openwebui.tf
    90→
    91→module "openwebui_lxc" {
    92→  source = "../modules/docker-host"
    93→
    94→  name          = "openwebui"
    95→  container_id  = 400
    96→  cores         = 2
    97→  memory        = 4096
    98→  disk_size     = 20
    99→
   100→  # Docker compose to deploy
   101→  compose_file  = "${path.root}/../podman/openwebui/docker-compose.yml"
   102→}
   103→
   104→module "openwebui_traefik" {
   105→  source = "../modules/traefik-route"
   106→
   107→  service_name  = "openwebui"
   108→  backend_host  = module.openwebui_lxc.ip_address
   109→  backend_port  = 3000
   110→
   111→  # Exposure configuration
   112→  domains = {
   113→    internal = "openwebui.homelab.rambtech.dev"
   114→    tailnet  = "openwebui.tailnet.rambtech.dev"
   115→  }
   116→
   117→  middlewares = ["security-headers", "internal-only"]
   118→}
   119→
   120→module "openwebui_public" {
   121→  source = "../modules/cloudflare-expose"
   122→  count  = var.expose_openwebui_publicly ? 1 : 0
   123→
   124→  service_name   = "openwebui"
   125→  domain         = "ai.rambtech.dev"
   126→  expose_type    = "tunnel"  # or "ddns"
   127→  tunnel_id      = module.core_cloudflared.tunnel_id
   128→  backend_url    = "http://${module.openwebui_lxc.ip_address}:3000"
   129→}
   130→
   131→module "openwebui_notes" {
   132→  source = "../modules/proxmox-notes"
   133→
   134→  container_id = module.openwebui_lxc.container_id
   135→  notes = <<-EOT
   136→    # OpenWebUI
   137→
   138→    ## Access
   139→    - Internal: https://openwebui.homelab.rambtech.dev
   140→    - Tailnet: https://openwebui.tailnet.rambtech.dev
   141→    ${var.expose_openwebui_publicly ? "- Public: https://ai.rambtech.dev" : ""}
   142→
   143→    ## Services
   144→    - OpenWebUI: Port 3000
   145→
   146→    ## Management
   147→    - SSH: ssh root@${module.openwebui_lxc.ip_address}
   148→    - Logs: podman logs openwebui
   149→  EOT
   150→}
   151→```
   152→
   153→## Module Implementations
   154→
   155→### 1. lxc-base module
   156→
   157→```hcl
   158→# modules/lxc-base/main.tf
   159→resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_container" "lxc" {
   160→  node_name    = var.proxmox_node
   161→  vm_id        = var.container_id
   162→  description  = var.description
   163→  tags         = var.tags
   164→
   165→  operating_system {
   166→    template_file_id = var.template
   167→    type             = "debian"
   168→  }
   169→
   170→  cpu {
   171→    cores = var.cores
   172→  }
   173→
   174→  memory {
   175→    dedicated = var.memory
   176→  }
   177→
   178→  disk {
   179→    datastore_id = var.storage
   180→    size         = var.disk_size
   181→  }
   182→
   183→  network_interface {
   184→    name   = "eth0"
   185→    bridge = "vmbr0"
   186→    # DHCP by default - we'll discover IP after creation
   187→  }
   188→
   189→  initialization {
   190→    hostname = var.name
   191→
   192→    user_account {
   193→      keys = [file(var.ssh_public_key)]
   194→    }
   195→  }
   196→
   197→  features {
   198→    nesting = var.enable_nesting  # Required for Docker
   199→    keyctl  = var.enable_keyctl   # Required for some containers
   200→  }
   201→
   202→  unprivileged = var.unprivileged
   203→  start_on_create = true
   204→}
   205→
   206→output "ip_address" {
   207→  value = proxmox_virtual_environment_container.lxc.initialization[0].ip_config[0].ipv4[0].address
   208→}
   209→
   210→output "container_id" {
   211→  value = proxmox_virtual_environment_container.lxc.vm_id
   212→}
   213→```
   214→
   215→### 2. docker-host module
   216→
   217→```hcl
   218→# modules/docker-host/main.tf
   219→module "lxc" {
   220→  source = "../lxc-base"
   221→
   222→  name           = var.name
   223→  container_id   = var.container_id
   224→  cores          = var.cores
   225→  memory         = var.memory
   226→  disk_size      = var.disk_size
   227→  enable_nesting = true  # Always needed for Docker
   228→  tags           = concat(var.tags, ["docker"])
   229→}
   230→
   231→# Wait for LXC to be ready
   232→resource "time_sleep" "wait_for_lxc" {
   233→  depends_on = [module.lxc]
   234→  create_duration = "30s"
   235→}
   236→
   237→# Provision Docker via Ansible
   238→resource "null_resource" "provision_docker" {
   239→  depends_on = [time_sleep.wait_for_lxc]
   240→
   241→  provisioner "local-exec" {
   242→    command = <<-EOT
   243→      ansible-playbook -i '${module.lxc.ip_address},' \
   244→        --private-key ~/.ssh/homelab_ed25519 \
   245→        -e ansible_user=root \
   246→        ${path.module}/playbooks/install-docker.yml
   247→    EOT
   248→  }
   249→}
   250→
   251→# Deploy compose file
   252→resource "null_resource" "deploy_compose" {
   253→  depends_on = [null_resource.provision_docker]
   254→
   255→  triggers = {
   256→    compose_hash = filemd5(var.compose_file)
   257→  }
   258→
   259→  provisioner "file" {
   260→    source      = var.compose_file
   261→    destination = "/config/docker-compose.yml"
   262→

# Homelab IaC Architecture Design

## Vision: Modular Service Deployment with Automatic Bindings

### Problem Statement

- Manual LXC creation via Proxmox UI or community scripts (xterm)
- Manual Traefik route configuration
- Manual Cloudflare tunnel/DNS setup
- No standardized way to add new services
- Hard to track what's running where

### Solution: Two-Tier Service Model with OpenTofu

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                           SERVICE TYPES                                     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  CORE SERVICES (Long-lived, foundational)                                   │
│  ├── traefik        → Ingress, TLS termination                              │
│  ├── cloudflared    → Public tunnel                                         │
│  ├── adguard        → DNS + ad blocking                                     │
│  ├── tailscale      → Mesh VPN                                              │
│  ├── pulse, arcane  → Container management                                  │
│  └── postgres       → Shared database (optional)                            │
│                                                                             │
│  APP SERVICES (User-facing applications)                                    │
│  ├── immich         → Photo management                                      │
│  ├── openwebui      → AI chat interface                                     │
│  ├── jellyfin       → Media streaming                                       │
│  ├── homepage       → Dashboard                                             │
│  └── ... any new service                                                    │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Architecture: Module-Based IaC

```
tofu/
├── main.tf                    # Root configuration
├── providers.tf               # Proxmox, Cloudflare providers
├── variables.tf               # Global variables
│
├── modules/
│   ├── lxc-base/              # Base LXC container module
│   │   ├── main.tf
│   │   ├── variables.tf
│   │   └── outputs.tf
│   │
│   ├── docker-host/           # LXC + Docker/Podman setup
│   │   ├── main.tf            # Calls lxc-base + provisions Docker
│   │   ├── variables.tf
│   │   └── outputs.tf
│   │
│   ├── traefik-route/         # Traefik ingress binding
│   │   ├── main.tf            # Creates route file, syncs to Traefik
│   │   ├── variables.tf       # service_name, port, domain, middlewares
│   │   └── outputs.tf         # route_url
│   │
│   ├── cloudflare-expose/     # Public exposure via tunnel or DNS
│   │   ├── main.tf            # DNS record or tunnel ingress rule
│   │   ├── variables.tf       # domain, expose_type (tunnel/ddns)
│   │   └── outputs.tf         # public_url
│   │
│   └── proxmox-notes/         # Update LXC description/notes
│       ├── main.tf            # pct set -description via SSH
│       └── variables.tf
│
├── core/                      # Core service definitions
│   ├── traefik.tf
│   ├── cloudflared.tf
│   ├── adguard.tf
│   └── tailscale.tf
│
└── apps/                      # Application definitions
    ├── immich.tf
    ├── openwebui.tf
    ├── jellyfin.tf
    └── homepage.tf
```

## Key Concept: Composable Service Module

When you want to add a new service, you just define it like this:

```hcl
# tofu/apps/openwebui.tf

module "openwebui_lxc" {
  source = "../modules/docker-host"

  name          = "openwebui"
  container_id  = 400
  cores         = 2
  memory        = 4096
  disk_size     = 20

  # Docker compose to deploy
  compose_file  = "${path.root}/../podman/openwebui/docker-compose.yml"
}

module "openwebui_traefik" {
  source = "../modules/traefik-route"

  service_name  = "openwebui"
  backend_host  = module.openwebui_lxc.ip_address
  backend_port  = 3000

  # Exposure configuration
  domains = {
    internal = "openwebui.homelab.rambtech.dev"
    tailnet  = "openwebui.tailnet.rambtech.dev"
  }

  middlewares = ["security-headers", "internal-only"]
}

module "openwebui_public" {
  source = "../modules/cloudflare-expose"
  count  = var.expose_openwebui_publicly ? 1 : 0

  service_name   = "openwebui"
  domain         = "ai.rambtech.dev"
  expose_type    = "tunnel"  # or "ddns"
  tunnel_id      = module.core_cloudflared.tunnel_id
  backend_url    = "http://${module.openwebui_lxc.ip_address}:3000"
}

module "openwebui_notes" {
  source = "../modules/proxmox-notes"

  container_id = module.openwebui_lxc.container_id
  notes = <<-EOT
    # OpenWebUI

    ## Access
    - Internal: https://openwebui.homelab.rambtech.dev
    - Tailnet: https://openwebui.tailnet.rambtech.dev
    ${var.expose_openwebui_publicly ? "- Public: https://ai.rambtech.dev" : ""}

    ## Services
    - OpenWebUI: Port 3000

    ## Management
    - SSH: ssh root@${module.openwebui_lxc.ip_address}
    - Logs: podman logs openwebui
  EOT
}
```

## Module Implementations

### 1. lxc-base module

```hcl
# modules/lxc-base/main.tf
resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_container" "lxc" {
  node_name    = var.proxmox_node
  vm_id        = var.container_id
  description  = var.description
  tags         = var.tags

  operating_system {
    template_file_id = var.template
    type             = "debian"
  }

  cpu {
    cores = var.cores
  }

  memory {
    dedicated = var.memory
  }

  disk {
    datastore_id = var.storage
    size         = var.disk_size
  }

  network_interface {
    name   = "eth0"
    bridge = "vmbr0"
    # DHCP by default - we'll discover IP after creation
  }

  initialization {
    hostname = var.name

    user_account {
      keys = [file(var.ssh_public_key)]
    }
  }

  features {
    nesting = var.enable_nesting  # Required for Docker
    keyctl  = var.enable_keyctl   # Required for some containers
  }

  unprivileged = var.unprivileged
  start_on_create = true
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = proxmox_virtual_environment_container.lxc.initialization[0].ip_config[0].ipv4[0].address
}

output "container_id" {
  value = proxmox_virtual_environment_container.lxc.vm_id
}
```

### 2. docker-host module

```hcl
# modules/docker-host/main.tf
module "lxc" {
  source = "../lxc-base"

  name           = var.name
  container_id   = var.container_id
  cores          = var.cores
  memory         = var.memory
  disk_size      = var.disk_size
  enable_nesting = true  # Always needed for Docker
  tags           = concat(var.tags, ["docker"])
}

# Wait for LXC to be ready
resource "time_sleep" "wait_for_lxc" {
  depends_on = [module.lxc]
  create_duration = "30s"
}

# Provision Docker via Ansible
resource "null_resource" "provision_docker" {
  depends_on = [time_sleep.wait_for_lxc]

  provisioner "local-exec" {
    command = <<-EOT
      ansible-playbook -i '${module.lxc.ip_address},' \
        --private-key ~/.ssh/homelab_ed25519 \
        -e ansible_user=root \
        ${path.module}/playbooks/install-docker.yml
    EOT
  }
}

# Deploy compose file
resource "null_resource" "deploy_compose" {
  depends_on = [null_resource.provision_docker]

  triggers = {
    compose_hash = filemd5(var.compose_file)
  }

  provisioner "file" {
    source      = var.compose_file
    destination = "/config/docker-compose.yml"

    connection {
      type        = "ssh"
      host        = module.lxc.ip_address
      user        = "root"
      private_key = file("~/.ssh/homelab_ed25519")
    }
  }

  provisioner "remote-exec" {
    inline = [
      "mkdir -p /config",
      "cd /config && docker compose up -d"
    ]

    connection {
      type        = "ssh"
      host        = module.lxc.ip_address
      user        = "root"
      private_key = file("~/.ssh/homelab_ed25519")
    }
  }
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.lxc.ip_address
}

output "container_id" {
  value = module.lxc.container_id
}
```

### 3. traefik-route module

```hcl

locals {
  route_config = {
    http = {
      routers = merge(
        {
          "${var.service_name}" = {

  }

  provisioner "local-exec" {
    command = <<-EOT
      ssh root@${var.proxmox_host} "pct set ${var.container_id} -description '${replace(var.notes, "'", "'\\''")}'"
    EOT
  }
}
```

## Handling Community Scripts

Since Proxmox community scripts need xterm, we use a hybrid approach:

### Option A: Pre-bake templates (for complex apps)
```bash
# Run once manually in Proxmox xterm console
bash -c "$(wget -qLO - https://github.com/community-scripts/ProxmoxVE/raw/main/ct/traefik.sh)"
# Then convert to template and use in Terraform
```

### Option B: Terraform + Ansible (recommended)
- Terraform creates vanilla Debian/Ubuntu LXC
- Ansible provisions Docker and services
- Fully automated, no xterm needed

## Providers Configuration

```hcl
# tofu/providers.tf
terraform {
  required_providers {
    proxmox = {
      source  = "bpg/proxmox"
      version = "~> 0.69"
    }
    cloudflare = {
      source  = "cloudflare/cloudflare"
      version = "~> 5"
    }
    local = {
      source  = "hashicorp/local"
      version = "~> 2.5"
    }
    null = {
      source  = "hashicorp/null"
      version = "~> 3.2"
    }
    time = {
      source  = "hashicorp/time"
      version = "~> 0.11"
    }
  }
}

provider "proxmox" {
  endpoint = var.proxmox_endpoint  # https://homelab:8006
  username = var.proxmox_username  # root@pam or API token
  password = var.proxmox_password
  insecure = true

  ssh {
    agent    = true
    username = "root"
  }
}

provider "cloudflare" {
  api_token = var.cloudflare_api_token
}
```

## Implementation Phases

### Phase 1: Foundation
- [ ] Set up OpenTofu project structure
- [ ] Create providers.tf (Proxmox, Cloudflare)
- [ ] Create lxc-base module
- [ ] Test with single LXC creation

### Phase 2: Core Services
- [ ] Create docker-host module
- [ ] Create traefik-route module
- [ ] Migrate existing Traefik LXC to IaC
- [ ] Test route auto-generation

### Phase 3: Cloudflare Integration
- [ ] Create cloudflare-expose module
- [ ] Import existing tunnel to Terraform state
- [ ] Test tunnel ingress rules

### Phase 4: App Migration
- [ ] Create app definition for one service (e.g., homepage)
- [ ] Migrate remaining apps incrementally
- [ ] Create proxmox-notes module

### Phase 5: Polish
- [ ] Add Taskfile integration
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] CI/CD for plan/apply

## New Taskfile Tasks

```yaml
# Add to Taskfile.yml
tofu:init:
  desc: "Initialize OpenTofu"
  dir: tofu
  cmds:
    - tofu init

tofu:plan:
  desc: "Plan infrastructure changes"
  dir: tofu
  cmds:
    - tofu plan

tofu:apply:
  desc: "Apply infrastructure changes"
  dir: tofu
  cmds:
    - tofu apply

tofu:destroy:
  desc: "Destroy infrastructure (use with caution)"
  dir: tofu
  cmds:
    - tofu destroy

app:create:
  desc: "Create a new app from template"
  cmds:
    - |
      echo "Creating app: {{.NAME}}"
      cp tofu/apps/_template.tf tofu/apps/{{.NAME}}.tf
      sed -i '' 's/APPNAME/{{.NAME}}/g' tofu/apps/{{.NAME}}.tf
      echo "Edit tofu/apps/{{.NAME}}.tf to configure your app"
  requires:
    vars: [NAME]
```

## Why OpenTofu over Pulumi

For this homelab use case:

| Aspect | OpenTofu | Pulumi |
|--------|----------|--------|
| Proxmox Provider | bpg/proxmox (excellent) | Built on bpg (same) |
| Cloudflare | First-class support | First-class support |
| Learning Curve | HCL is simple | Need Python/TS |
| Community | Larger, more examples | Growing |
| State | Local/S3/TF Cloud | Pulumi Service |
| License | Open source (MPL 2.0) | Open source |

**Recommendation: OpenTofu** - simpler for infrastructure-focused work.

## Questions to Clarify

1. Do you want to use existing LXC IDs or let Terraform assign new ones?
2. Should we import existing infrastructure or start fresh?
3. Preference for state backend (local, S3, Terraform Cloud)?
4. Which service should we migrate first as a proof of concept?

# Homelab Backup Strategy

## Overview

Two-tier backup system with daily backups for user data services and weekly backups for infrastructure. All backups are synced to Backblaze B2 (encrypted) for off-site redundancy.

## Backup Tiers

### Daily Backups (2:00 AM)

User data that changes frequently - kept for 7 days.

| ID | Service | Pre-Backup Hook |
|----|---------|-----------------|
| 304 | Immich | PostgreSQL dump |
| 501 | OpenWebUI | SQLite copy |
| 502 | n8n | SQLite copy |

### Weekly Backups (Sunday 3:00 AM)

Infrastructure services that rarely change - kept for 4 weeks.

| ID | Service | Pre-Backup Hook |
|----|---------|-----------------|
| 101 | Network Services (AdGuard) | None |
| 200 | Traefik | None |
| 201 | Dashboards | None |
| 202 | Authelia | None |
| 401 | Jellyfin | Jellystat PostgreSQL dump |
| 402 | Media Management | None |
| 500 | Monitoring | None |

### Excluded Containers

- **303 (immich-importer)** - Stateless, runs cron jobs only
- **600 (desktop-tmp)** - Temporary GUI container

## Cloud Backup (Backblaze B2)

All local backups are synced to Backblaze B2 with rclone crypt encryption.

| Sync | Schedule | Source | Destination |
|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| Photos | Daily 3:00 AM | LXC 303 `/photos` | `b2-crypt:` |
| Vzdump | Daily 4:00 AM | `/tank/backups/vzdump` | `b2-crypt:vzdump` |
| DB Dumps | Daily 4:00 AM | `/tank/backups/database-dumps` | `b2-crypt:database-dumps` |

### Daily Timeline

```text
2:00 AM - Daily vzdump backups (immich, openwebui, n8n)
3:00 AM - Photos cloud sync to B2
4:00 AM - Vzdump + DB dumps cloud sync to B2
```

## Storage Layout

```text
/tank/backups/
├── vzdump/dump/           # Proxmox vzdump backups
│   ├── vzdump-lxc-100-*.tar.zst
│   ├── vzdump-lxc-101-*.tar.zst
│   └── ...
└── database-dumps/        # Pre-backup database dumps
    ├── immich-postgres-*.sql.gz
    ├── jellystat-postgres-*.sql.gz
    ├── openwebui-*.db
    └── n8n-*.db
```

## Taskfile Commands

### Local Backups

```bash
# Sync backup config to Proxmox
task backup:sync

# View status
task backup:status

# Manual backups
task backup:now APP=openwebui    # Single container
task backup:all                   # All containers

# List backups for an app
task backup:list APP=immich

# Restore container
task backup:restore BACKUP=vzdump-lxc-304-2025_12_07-02_00_00.tar.zst TARGET_ID=305

# Immich database operations
task backup:immich:db              # Manual dump
task backup:immich:db:restore DUMP=immich-postgres-20251207_020000.sql.gz
```

### Cloud Backups

```bash
# Trigger cloud sync
task cloud:sync              # Both vzdump + photos
task cloud:sync:vzdump       # Vzdump only
task cloud:sync:photos       # Photos only

# Check status
task cloud:status            # B2 bucket sizes
task cloud:status:photos     # Photos backup status
task cloud:progress          # Check if sync is running
task cloud:dry-run           # Preview what would sync

# View logs
task cloud:logs              # Vzdump sync logs
task cloud:logs:photos       # Photos sync logs
```

## Restore Procedures

### Full Container Restore

```bash
# 1. List available backups
task backup:list APP=openwebui

# 2. Restore to new container ID (recommended for testing)
task backup:restore BACKUP=vzdump-lxc-501-2025_12_10-19_28_32.tar.zst TARGET_ID=505

# 3. Verify restored container
ssh root@homelab "pct start 505"

# 4. If verified, swap with original:
#    - Stop original (501)
#    - Update network config on new container
#    - Start new container
```

### Database-Only Restore

```bash
# Immich PostgreSQL
task backup:immich:db:restore DUMP=immich-postgres-20251207_020000.sql.gz

# Other databases - manual restore from /tank/backups/database-dumps/
ssh root@homelab "ls -lh /tank/backups/database-dumps/"
```

### Extract Files from Backup

```bash
ssh root@homelab
cd /tmp
tar -xf /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-501-2025_12_10-19_28_32.tar.zst
# Navigate and extract needed files
```

## Monitoring

### Check Backup Status

```bash
# View scheduled jobs
ssh root@homelab "cat /etc/pve/jobs.cfg"

# View hook script logs
ssh root@homelab "tail -50 /var/log/vzdump-hooks.log"

# Check local storage usage
task backup:status

# Check cloud backup status
task cloud:status
```

### Proxmox UI

Backup jobs visible at: **Datacenter > Backup**

## Files Reference

| File | Location | Purpose |
|------|----------|---------|
| Job config (source) | `scripts/backup/jobs.cfg` | Scheduled vzdump job definitions |
| Hook script (source) | `scripts/backup/pre-backup-hook.sh` | Pre-backup database dumps |
| Job config (deployed) | `/etc/pve/jobs.cfg` | Synced via `task backup:sync` |
| Hook script (deployed) | `/var/lib/vz/snippets/pre-backup-hook.sh` | Synced via `task backup:sync` |
| Hook log | `/var/log/vzdump-hooks.log` | Hook script output |
| Cloud sync script | `/root/cloud-sync.sh` | Vzdump to B2 sync (on Proxmox) |
| Photos sync script | `/usr/local/bin/cloud-sync.sh` | Photos to B2 sync (on LXC 303) |

## Adding New Containers

1. Edit `scripts/backup/jobs.cfg`:
   - Add container ID to `daily-user-data` (for user data) or `weekly-infrastructure` (for infra)
2. Edit `scripts/backup/backup-app.sh` and `scripts/backup/backup-list.sh`:
   - Add the app name to container ID mapping
3. (Optional) If container has a database, edit `scripts/backup/pre-backup-hook.sh`:
   - Add a dump function and case in `backup-start`
4. Run `task backup:sync` to deploy configs to Proxmox

## Database Notes

### Immich (304)

- PostgreSQL with pgvecto-rs extension (ML embeddings)
- Container: `immich_postgres`
- Dumps kept 7 days

### Jellystat (401)

- PostgreSQL 15 for Jellyfin statistics
- Container: `jellystat-db`
- User/DB: `jellystat`
- Dumps kept 4 weeks

### OpenWebUI (501)

- SQLite at `/config/openwebui/webui.db`
- Contains chat history, users, settings
- Copied directly (no sqlite3 in container)

### n8n (502)

- SQLite at `/config/n8n/database.sqlite`
- Contains workflows, credentials, execution history

     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→This document outlines procedures for recovering the homelab from various failure scenarios. For detailed backup information, see [backups.md](./backups.md).
     6→
     7→## Quick Reference
     8→
     9→| Scenario | RTO | RPO | Procedure |
    10→| -------- | --- | --- | --------- |
    11→| Single container failure | 15 min | < 24 hrs | [Container Recovery](#single-container-recovery) |
    12→| Proxmox host failure | 2-4 hrs | < 24 hrs | [Full Host Recovery](#full-host-recovery) |
    13→| Database corruption | 30 min | < 24 hrs | [Database Recovery](#database-recovery) |
    14→| Network services down | 5 min | N/A | [Network Recovery](#network-services-recovery) |
    15→
    16→## Service Dependencies
    17→
    18→### Recovery Order (Critical Path)
    19→
    20→Recovery must follow this order due to service dependencies:
    21→
    22→```text
    23→1. Proxmox VE host
    24→   └── 2. Network Services (LXC 101) - AdGuard DNS
    25→       └── 3. Traefik (LXC 200) - Reverse proxy
    26→           └── 4. Authelia (LXC 202) - SSO/Auth
    27→               └── 5. All other services
    28→```
    29→
    30→### Tier 1: Infrastructure (Recover First)
    31→
    32→| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies | Critical For |
    33→| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ | ------------ |
    34→| - | Proxmox VE | 192.168.1.215 | None | Everything |
    35→| 101 | Network Services | 10.100.1.101 / 192.168.1.196 | Proxmox | DNS resolution |
    36→| 200 | Traefik | 10.100.2.200 / 192.168.1.235 | DNS | HTTPS access to all services |
    37→| 202 | Authelia | 10.100.2.202 | Traefik | Protected service access |
    38→
    39→### Tier 2: Core Services
    40→
    41→| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
    42→| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
    43→| 500 | Monitoring | 10.100.5.100 | Traefik |
    44→| 201 | Dashboards | 10.100.2.201 | Traefik |
    45→
    46→### Tier 3: Application Services
    47→
    48→| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
    49→| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
    50→| 304 | Immich | 10.100.3.104 / 192.168.1.222 | Traefik, Authelia |
    51→| 401 | Jellyfin | 10.100.4.101 / 192.168.1.226 | Traefik |
    52→| 402 | Media Management | 10.100.4.102 | Traefik, Authelia, VPN (gluetun) |
    53→| 501 | OpenWebUI | 10.100.5.101 | Traefik, Authelia |
    54→| 502 | n8n | 10.100.5.102 | Traefik, Authelia |
    55→| 503 | Obsidian Sync | 10.100.5.103 | Traefik |
    56→| 504 | Documents | 10.100.5.104 | Traefik, Authelia |
    57→
    58→### Stateless Services (No Backup Required)
    59→
    60→| ID | Service | Notes |
    61→| -- | ------- | ----- |
    62→| 303 | Immich Importer | Stateless uploader. Auto-starts with Proxmox. No data to backup. |
    63→
    64→## Recovery Procedures
    65→
    66→### Single Container Recovery
    67→
    68→*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
    69→This uses PBS (Proxmox Backup Server) incremental backups with OpenTofu for infrastructure recreation.
    70→
    71→#### Step 1: Prepare for Recreation
    72→
    73→Get the IP address, remove the old SSH host key, and rename the state file. This ensures OpenTofu recreates all resources and can connect to the new LXC without mid-apply failures.
    74→
    75→```bash
    76→cd tofu/apps/<APP>
    77→
    78→# Get IP before renaming state (so tofu output still works)
    79→IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    80→
    81→# Remove old SSH key (prevents host key mismatch during apply)
    82→[ -n "$IP" ] && ssh-keygen -R $IP
    83→
    84→# Rename state to force full recreation
    85→mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old
    86→```
    87→
    88→#### Step 2: Recreate Infrastructure
    89→
    90→```bash
    91→task tofu:init APP=<APP>
    92→task tofu:apply APP=<APP>
    93→```
    94→
    95→This will:
    96→
    97→- Create new LXC container with same VMID
    98→- Run Ansible to configure base system
    99→- Deploy docker-compose and config files
   100→- Start Docker containers (with empty/fresh data)
   101→- Configure PBS backup client
   102→- Deploy Pulse/Arcane agents
   103→
   104→#### Step 3: Restore Data from PBS
   105→
   106→```bash
   107→task pbs:backup:restore APP=<APP>
   108→```
   109→
   110→This will:

# Disaster Recovery Runbook

## Overview

This document outlines procedures for recovering the homelab from various failure scenarios. For detailed backup information, see [backups.md](./backups.md).

## Quick Reference

| Scenario | RTO | RPO | Procedure |
| -------- | --- | --- | --------- |
| Single container failure | 15 min | < 24 hrs | [Container Recovery](#single-container-recovery) |
| Proxmox host failure | 2-4 hrs | < 24 hrs | [Full Host Recovery](#full-host-recovery) |
| Database corruption | 30 min | < 24 hrs | [Database Recovery](#database-recovery) |
| Network services down | 5 min | N/A | [Network Recovery](#network-services-recovery) |

## Service Dependencies

### Recovery Order (Critical Path)

Recovery must follow this order due to service dependencies:

```text
1. Proxmox VE host
   └── 2. Network Services (LXC 101) - AdGuard DNS
       └── 3. Traefik (LXC 200) - Reverse proxy
           └── 4. Authelia (LXC 202) - SSO/Auth
               └── 5. All other services
```

### Tier 1: Infrastructure (Recover First)

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies | Critical For |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ | ------------ |
| - | Proxmox VE | 192.168.1.215 | None | Everything |
| 101 | Network Services | 10.100.1.101 / 192.168.1.196 | Proxmox | DNS resolution |
| 200 | Traefik | 10.100.2.200 / 192.168.1.235 | DNS | HTTPS access to all services |
| 202 | Authelia | 10.100.2.202 | Traefik | Protected service access |

### Tier 2: Core Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 500 | Monitoring | 10.100.5.100 | Traefik |
| 201 | Dashboards | 10.100.2.201 | Traefik |

### Tier 3: Application Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 304 | Immich | 10.100.3.104 / 192.168.1.222 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 401 | Jellyfin | 10.100.4.101 / 192.168.1.226 | Traefik |
| 402 | Media Management | 10.100.4.102 | Traefik, Authelia, VPN (gluetun) |
| 501 | OpenWebUI | 10.100.5.101 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 502 | n8n | 10.100.5.102 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 503 | Obsidian Sync | 10.100.5.103 | Traefik |
| 504 | Documents | 10.100.5.104 | Traefik, Authelia |

### Stateless Services (No Backup Required)

| ID | Service | Notes |
| -- | ------- | ----- |
| 303 | Immich Importer | Stateless uploader. Auto-starts with Proxmox. No data to backup. |

## Recovery Procedures

### Single Container Recovery

*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
This uses PBS (Proxmox Backup Server) incremental backups with OpenTofu for infrastructure recreation.

#### Step 1: Prepare for Recreation

Get the IP address, remove the old SSH host key, and rename the state file. This ensures OpenTofu recreates all resources and can connect to the new LXC without mid-apply failures.

```bash
cd tofu/apps/<APP>

# Get IP before renaming state (so tofu output still works)
IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address 2>/dev/null || echo "")

# Remove old SSH key (prevents host key mismatch during apply)
[ -n "$IP" ] && ssh-keygen -R $IP

# Rename state to force full recreation
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Step 2: Recreate Infrastructure

```bash
task tofu:init APP=<APP>
task tofu:apply APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Create new LXC container with same VMID
- Run Ansible to configure base system
- Deploy docker-compose and config files
- Start Docker containers (with empty/fresh data)
- Configure PBS backup client
- Deploy Pulse/Arcane agents

#### Step 3: Restore Data from PBS

```bash
task pbs:backup:restore APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Stop Docker containers
- Restore `/config` directory from PBS backup
- Restore Docker volume data from PBS backup
- Start Docker containers

#### Step 4: Verify and Cleanup

1. Check the app is working at its URL
1. Verify data is restored correctly
1. (Optional) Compare state files to verify same resources are tracked:

```bash
# Compare resource lists between old and new state (no output = match)
diff <(task tofu:state APP=<APP>) <(task tofu:state APP=<APP> -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old)
```

1. Clean up old state file:

```bash
rm terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Example: Recovering n8n

```bash
cd tofu/apps/n8n

# 1. Prepare (get IP, remove SSH key, rename state)
IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address)
ssh-keygen -R $IP
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old

# 2. Recreate
task tofu:init APP=n8n
task tofu:apply APP=n8n

# 3. Restore data
task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n

# 4. Verify app is working
curl -s http://10.100.5.102:5678/healthz
# Should return: {"status":"ok"}

# 5. Verify state matches (no output = success)
diff <(task tofu:state APP=n8n) <(task tofu:state APP=n8n -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old)

# 6. Cleanup
rm terraform.tfstate.old
```

### Database Recovery

#### Immich (PostgreSQL with pgvecto-rs)

```bash
# 1. List available dumps
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "ls -lh /tank/backups/database-dumps/immich-postgres-*"

# 2. Restore using task
task backup:immich:db:restore DUMP=immich-postgres-20251207_020000.sql.gz
```

#### Jellystat (PostgreSQL)

```bash
# 1. Copy dump to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 401 /tank/backups/database-dumps/jellystat-postgres-*.sql.gz /tmp/"

# 2. SSH to Jellyfin container
ssh root@10.100.4.101

# 3. Restore
docker exec -i jellystat-db psql -U jellystat -d jellystat < /tmp/jellystat-postgres-*.sql
```

#### SQLite Databases (OpenWebUI, n8n)

```bash
# Copy from backup dump directory to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 501 /tank/backups/database-dumps/openwebui-*.db /config/openwebui/webui.db"

# Restart the service
ssh root@10.100.5.101 "cd /config && docker compose restart"
```

### Network Services Recovery

If DNS (AdGuard) is down, LAN devices cannot resolve homelab domains.

1. **Temporary workaround** - Use direct IPs:
   - Proxmox: <https://192.168.1.215:8006>
   - Traefik: <http://192.168.1.235:8080> (dashboard)

2. **Recover AdGuard container**

   ```bash
   # Check container status
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct status 101"

   # Start if stopped
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start 101"

   # Check AdGuard service
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "docker ps"
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "cd /config && docker compose up -d"
   ```

3. **Verify DNS resolution**

   ```bash
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

### Full Host Recovery

This procedure assumes complete Proxmox host failure requiring reinstall.

#### Phase 1: Proxmox Installation (30 min)

1. Boot from Proxmox ISO
2. Install to boot drive
3. Configure network:
   - IP: 192.168.1.215/24
   - Gateway: 192.168.1.1
   - DNS: 1.1.1.1 (temporarily)
4. Import ZFS pool:

   ```bash
   zpool import tank
   ```

#### Phase 2: Restore Configuration (30 min)

1. Clone the homelab repo:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/darshan-rambhia/proxmox-homelab.git
   cd homelab
   ```

2. Sync backup configuration:

   ```bash
   task backup:sync
   ```

3. Restore containers from local backups (if ZFS pool survived):

   ```bash
   # List available backups
   ls /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/

   # Restore each container - start with Tier 1
   pct restore 101 /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-101-*.tar.zst
   pct restore 200 /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-200-*.tar.zst
   # ... continue for all containers
   ```

#### Phase 3: Cloud Recovery (if local backups lost)

If ZFS pool is lost, restore from Backblaze B2 (offshore backup location):

> **Note:** This procedure has not been fully tested end-to-end. See `proxmox-homelab-vig` for testing task.

1. Install rclone and configure with existing credentials from 1Password:

   ```bash
   apt install rclone
   # Get rclone config from 1Password vault "homelab"
   # Configure b2 and b2-crypt remotes with encryption keys
   ```

2. List available backups to verify connectivity:

   ```bash
   rclone ls b2-crypt:vzdump/ --max-depth 1
   rclone ls b2-crypt:database-dumps/ --max-depth 1
   ```

3. Download backups (this may take hours depending on data size):

   ```bash
   # Download vzdump container backups
   rclone copy b2-crypt:vzdump /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/ --progress

   # Download database dumps
   rclone copy b2-crypt:database-dumps /tank/backups/database-dumps/ --progress
   ```

4. Restore containers as in Phase 2

#### Phase 4: Verification (30 min)

1. Start containers in dependency order:

   ```bash
   pct start 101  # Network Services
   pct start 200  # Traefik
   pct start 202  # Authelia
   # ... rest of containers
   ```

2. Verify services:

   ```bash
   # DNS
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev

   # Web services
   curl -k https://homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

3. Re-apply OpenTofu if needed:

   ```bash
   task tofu:init APP=traefik
   task tofu:plan APP=traefik
   # Review and apply if needed
   ```

## Verification Checklist

After any recovery, verify:

### Tier 1: Infrastructure to verify

- [ ] DNS resolution working (`dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev`)
- [ ] Traefik dashboard accessible (<https://traefik.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
- [ ] Authelia login working

### Tier 2: Core Services to verify

- [ ] Homepage loads and shows service status
- [ ] Monitoring (Grafana) showing metrics

### Tier 3: Application Services to verify

- [ ] Immich accessible and photos loading
- [ ] Jellyfin accessible and library visible (<https://jellyfin.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
- [ ] n8n healthcheck passing (`curl -s http://10.100.5.102:5678/healthz`)
- [ ] Obsidian Sync accessible (<https://obsidian.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
- [ ] Documents (Paperless) accessible (<https://docs.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
- [ ] OpenWebUI accessible (<https://ai.homelab.rambtech.dev>)

### System Health

- [ ] Backups scheduled (`cat /etc/pve/jobs.cfg`)
- [ ] PBS backup timers active (`task pbs:backup:status APP=<app>`)

## Preventive Measures

### Regular Testing

- Monthly: Test restore of one container to verify backups
- Quarterly: Full DR drill - document actual recovery time

### Monitoring Gaps to Address

- [ ] Add backup failure alerting (see proxmox-homelab-v9t)
- [ ] Add Prometheus scrape targets for all services (see proxmox-homelab-30m)

## Contact & Escalation

For issues beyond this runbook:

- Proxmox Forums: <https://forum.proxmox.com/>
- Backblaze Support: <https://www.backblaze.com/help/>
